messages.subject: total copy number analysis(5.0 &6.0) questiones
parts:
Hi, i am new to the field so my question may be really naive.

I am trying to do copy number estimantion on 7 sample of affymetrix
snp 6.0 and I followed the instruction of the following link:
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis-6-0

Everything works fine but towards the end I got confused:

"rawCNs <- extractRawCopyNumbers(cbs, array=1, chromosome=1)
With the above setup, we could have called:
fit(cbs, arrays=1:2, chromosomes=c(19, 22), verbose=verbose)
to do segmentation on Chr19 and Chr22 of the first and second arrays.
The
estimated copy-number regions would have been stored in files under
cbsData/. However, we are next going to display the raw CNs and the
segmentation results in the ChromosomeExplorer. As we will see, when
asking the explorer to process a certain array and chromosome, it will
in turn
ask the segmentation model to fit that same data, if not already
fitted. So, we
take the following shortcut.
To fit CBS and at the same time generate graphical output for, say,
chromosome 19, 22, and 23 (X), do:
ce <- ChromosomeExplorer(cbs)"

Say I want to take the short cut to get the estimation and report
through
ce <- chrmosomeExplorer(cbs).

where can I put the list of sample and chromosom in the function?
And if I want to simply process all samples all chromosom, what do I
do?

Thanks,
Yupu

messages.author: 9dda904b2c7a149c
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] total copy number analysis(5.0 &6.0) questiones
parts:
Hi,

If I understand you correctly, it looks like you are asking how to get
the segmentation results for all arrays and all chromosomes (correct
me if I'm wrong) and also to display the results, rather than fitting
separately. To do this just use the following code:

ce <- ChromosomeExplorer(cbs)
process(ce, arrays=1:7, chromosomes=1:23, verbose=verbose)
display(ce)

Note that this may take some time, so be prepared to wait.

I think I see where you have got confused with the vignette - we'll
update to make it a bit clearer.

Cheers

Ken
